epics: Establish secure authentication flow into NetSuite (supporting SSO and direct credentials)
Configure identity provider integration (SAML/OIDC) and service provider settings in NetSuite
Implement user provisioning, role assignment and mapping between corporate directory and NetSuite roles
Enforce authentication security controls: MFA, password policy, session timeouts and account lockout
Add logging, monitoring and audit trails for login attempts, failures and administrative changes
Provide user-facing error messages, self-service password recovery/workflow and admin tools for account unlocks
analysis.storiesSummary: Implement a secure, auditable login capability for NetSuite that supports corporate SSO (SAML/OIDC) and fallback credential-based authentication. Stories cover configuring the identity provider and NetSuite as service provider, automatic or manual user provisioning and role mapping, enforcing MFA and password/session policies, exposing clear error and recovery flows for end users, and capturing logs/alerts for security and compliance monitoring.
risks: Misconfiguration of SSO (SAML/OIDC) could lock out users or allow unauthorized access
Insecure storage or transmission of credentials/API keys if direct credential flows are used
Mismatch between corporate directory roles and NetSuite roles leading to excessive or insufficient privileges
Lack of MFA or weak password policies increasing risk of account compromise
Insufficient logging/monitoring hindering incident detection and compliance reporting
Network/firewall or IP restrictions preventing successful connections to NetSuite or IdP
API/rate limits or environment differences (sandbox vs production) causing integration failures
User experience issues or unclear error messages causing support overhead and increased helpdesk tickets
assumptions: Organization has an active NetSuite account with administrative access to configure SSO and roles
An identity provider (e.g., Okta, Azure AD) is available or will be provided for SSO integration
Required NetSuite modules/licensing and API access permissions are available
Stakeholders will provide mapping of corporate roles/groups to NetSuite roles and required access levels
MFA policy requirements are defined and supported by the chosen IdP or NetSuite configuration
Network connectivity and firewall rules will permit outbound/inbound SAML/OIDC and API traffic to NetSuite
Test and sandbox NetSuite environments exist for development and QA before production roll-out
Users who require self-service password recovery are covered by the organization’s identity provider or support processes

milestones.name: Discovery & Requirements
milestones.description: Gather functional and non-functional requirements for NetSuite login (users, roles, access patterns, security/compliance needs, SSO vs token-based, user provisioning).

milestones.name: Account and Environment Setup
milestones.description: Provision NetSuite sandbox accounts, create admin/test users, configure roles and permissions needed for development and testing.

milestones.name: Authentication Method Selection & Design
milestones.description: Decide on authentication approach (SuiteSignOn/SAML SSO, OAuth 2.0, Token-based integration, or credentials), design flow, and document endpoints, certificates, and token lifetimes.

milestones.name: Integration Development
milestones.description: Implement authentication integration (SSO/SP Federation or OAuth/token exchange), build connector or configuration scripts, and integrate with identity provider if required.

milestones.name: Configuration: NetSuite & IdP
milestones.description: Configure NetSuite settings (SSO, access tokens, role mapping) and configure Identity Provider (metadata, certificates, attribute mapping).

milestones.name: Testing & QA
milestones.description: Execute functional, integration, regression, and negative tests (password resets, session expiry, role enforcement), plus cross-browser and device checks.

milestones.name: Security Review & Compliance Validation
milestones.description: Perform security assessment (vulnerabilities, token handling, certificate validation), review audit logging, and confirm compliance requirements are met.

milestones.name: Documentation & Training
milestones.description: Produce user-facing login guides, admin setup guides, runbooks for support, and deliver training sessions to admins and support staff.

milestones.name: Deployment & Rollout
milestones.description: Promote configuration and integration to production, perform smoke tests, and execute planned cutover (including rollback plan).

milestones.name: Post-deployment Monitoring & Support
milestones.description: Monitor login metrics, error rates, user feedback; triage issues and deploy fixes; perform a post-launch review.

functionSpecs.userStory: As an end user, I want to log in to NetSuite with my username and password so that I can access my account and perform my daily tasks.
outputs: HTTP status code and JSON payload with user profile and default role (on success)
constraints: Passwords must be validated against NetSuite-backed authentication service using secure channel (TLS 1.2+).
Rate limit failed login attempts per account and per IP to prevent brute force (e.g., 5 attempts/15 minutes).
Do not return detailed reasons about password vs username mismatch to avoid account enumeration.
Session token TTL must comply with NetSuite session policies.
All sensitive data in transit and at rest must be encrypted per organizational policy.
acceptanceCriteria: Given valid username/password, when user submits credentials, then the system returns HTTP 200 and a valid session token and user profile.
Given invalid credentials, when user submits credentials, then the system returns HTTP 401 with a generic authentication failure message.
Given repeated failed attempts exceeding the limit, when user continues to try, then account lockout or progressive delay is enforced.
Given rememberMe true, when authentication succeeds, then a persistent, secure cookie or long-lived token is issued following policy.

functionSpecs.userStory: As an enterprise user, I want to sign in to NetSuite using Single Sign-On (SSO) so that I can use our corporate identity provider and avoid managing separate credentials.
inputs: SAML assertion or OAuth ID token from corporate IdP
outputs: NetSuite session created and redirect to requested resource (on success)
constraints: Support SAML 2.0 and/or OAuth 2.0 as per NetSuite supported protocols.
Validate assertions/tokens (signature, issuer, audience, expiration) before granting access.
Certificates and trust anchors must be managed securely and rotated per policy.
Mapping between IdP attributes and NetSuite user accounts/roles must be configurable.
Ensure replay protection for assertions (use InResponseTo and timestamps).
acceptanceCriteria: Given valid SAML/OAuth assertion from trusted IdP, when processed, then user is authenticated and redirected to their NetSuite landing page.
Given invalid or expired assertion, when processed, then authentication fails and an appropriate error is logged and returned.
Given new user assertion with mapped attributes, when mapping creates or links account, then user receives the correct NetSuite role as configured.
Given certificate rotation on IdP, when new certificate is in use, then authentication continues after updating trust anchors without service disruption.

functionSpecs.userStory: As a security-conscious user, I want multi-factor authentication (MFA) at login so that my account is protected even if my password is compromised.
inputs: MFA method selection (SMS, authenticator app, hardware token)
constraints: MFA enrollment must be completed before enforcement; allow admin policy for required/enforced MFA.
OTP validation must tolerate small clock skew for TOTP (e.g., ±30s window) but prevent reuse.
Do not transmit OTPs in logs or non-secure channels.
Fallback/backup methods must be available (recovery codes, admin reset) and audited.
SMS is less secure; use only if allowed by policy and require fallback enrollment.
acceptanceCriteria: Given account with MFA enabled, when valid username/password are entered, then system prompts for MFA and accepts valid OTP to create session.
Given invalid or expired MFA code, when submitted, then authentication is denied and a limited number of retries are allowed.
Given user not enrolled in MFA and policy requires it, when user attempts login, then they are guided through enrollment or denied per policy.
Given use of recovery code, when valid recovery code is used, then access is granted and the recovery code is invalidated.

functionSpecs.userStory: As a user who forgot their password, I want to reset my NetSuite password securely so that I can regain access to my account without help desk intervention.
inputs: password reset token (from email) and new password
optional secondary verification (e.g., security questions or MFA)
outputs: password reset request acceptance (email sent) or failure
password reset confirmation page or message
audit log entry for reset request and completion
constraints: Reset tokens must be cryptographically random, one-time use, and expire within a short window (e.g., 1 hour).
Emails should not reveal whether an account exists; use consistent generic messaging where required by policy.
New passwords must meet NetSuite password complexity rules and not be reused within defined history.
Rate limit reset requests per account/IP to prevent abuse.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a valid username/email, when requesting a password reset, then an email with a secure reset link is sent and the request is logged.
Given expired or tampered token, when used to reset password, then reset is denied and user is prompted to request again.
Given valid reset token and compliant new password, when submitted, then password is updated and user can authenticate with the new password.
Given multiple reset requests, when subsequent requests are made, then only the most recent token remains valid.

functionSpecs.userStory: As a user with multiple roles, I want to select my NetSuite role after logging in so that I see the correct dashboard and permissions for my current task.
inputs: list of roles assigned to the user
optional preference flag to remember role selection
outputs: error if role is no longer available
constraints: Role assignments are determined by NetSuite role mappings and must be checked at login time.
Remembered role preference should expire or be revokable by the user/admin.
switching roles must validate current session privileges and not elevate permissions beyond allowed roles.
Role change actions should be audited.
acceptanceCriteria: Given user with multiple roles, when login completes, then the system prompts to choose a role and navigates to the correct dashboard.
Given user selects a role to remember, when subsequent logins occur, then the remembered role is preselected unless overridden or revoked.
Given role removed by admin, when user tries to select that role, then an error is shown and the available roles list is refreshed.
Given role change during an active session, when user switches roles, then permissions update immediately and action is logged.

functionSpecs.userStory: As an administrator, I want session management controls (timeout and logout) so that idle sessions are ended and active sessions can be terminated for security.
inputs: session token and last activity timestamp
admin session termination request (session ID or user ID)
configurable timeout policy (inactivity and absolute max session duration)
outputs: redirect to login page upon logout/timeout
HTTP 401 for requests using invalidated tokens
constraints: Idle timeout and absolute session TTL must follow NetSuite and organizational policies.
Token revocation must propagate quickly across all app servers and integrations.
Graceful handling of in-flight API calls when sessions are invalidated.
Ensure logout clears authentication cookies and client-side storage.
acceptanceCriteria: Given idle session exceeding inactivity timeout, when next request arrives, then session is invalidated and user is redirected to login.
Given admin terminates a session, when termination is executed, then further requests using that session are rejected with 401.
Given user explicitly logs out, when logout completes, then session token is revoked and browser cookies cleared.
Given session TTL policy change, when policy is updated, then new sessions comply immediately and existing sessions are handled per migration plan.

functionSpecs.userStory: As a security officer, I want all login attempts and authentication events logged and monitored so that we can audit access and detect suspicious activity for NetSuite accounts.
inputs: authentication attempt metadata (username, timestamp, IP, user agent, outcome)
admin actions related to authentication (locks, resets)
outputs: structured audit logs (secure, immutable store) with event types
real-time alerts for suspicious patterns (multiple failures, geo-anomalies)
regular reports on login activity and policy compliance
constraints: Logs must not contain plaintext secrets (passwords, OTPs).
Retention and access control for logs must meet compliance requirements.
Log format must be parsable by SIEM and include correlation IDs.
Alert thresholds must be tunable to reduce false positives.
acceptanceCriteria: Given any authentication event, when it occurs, then a corresponding structured log entry is written within defined SLA (e.g., <5s).
Given multiple failed logins from different IPs for same account, when threshold exceeded, then an alert is generated to the security team.
Given audit log query for a user and date range, when executed, then all authentication events are returned and linkable to session IDs and outcomes.
Given access requests to audit logs, when requested, then access is controlled by role-based permissions and successfully enforced.

files.contents:
Minimal scaffold demonstrating core flows to "Login into NetSuite".

Two minimal approaches are illustrated:

1) SOAP Passport login (SuiteTalk SOAP / legacy Passport) - POST a SOAP envelope with credentials to the NetSuite SOAP endpoint.

2) Token-Based Authentication (TBA) - use OAuth 1.0 credentials (consumer key/secret + token id/secret) to sign REST requests.

Files:
- .env.example : environment variables used by the examples.
- src/login_netsuite.py : minimal Python example implementing both flows.

These are intentionally small and illustrative. Replace placeholders with your account data and secrets before use.

### SOAP / Passport
NS_ACCOUNT=1234567
NS_EMAIL=you@example.com
NS_PASSWORD=YourPassword
NS_ROLE_INTERNALID=3   # optional

### Token Based Authentication (TBA)
NS_CONSUMER_KEY=your_consumer_key
NS_CONSUMER_SECRET=your_consumer_secret
NS_TOKEN_ID=your_token_id
NS_TOKEN_SECRET=your_token_secret

### Common
NS_AUTH_METHOD=SOAP  # or TBA
NS_SOAP_VERSION=2022_2  # used to build endpoint (example)

import os
import requests
from requests_oauthlib import OAuth1

# Small, focused example showing two ways to authenticate to NetSuite.
#  - SOAP Passport (SuiteTalk SOAP)
#  - Token-Based Authentication (TBA) for REST

# Load from environment
ACCOUNT = os.getenv("NS_ACCOUNT")
AUTH_METHOD = os.getenv("NS_AUTH_METHOD", "SOAP").upper()
SOAP_VERSION = os.getenv("NS_SOAP_VERSION", "2022_2")

# SOAP credentials
EMAIL = os.getenv("NS_EMAIL")
PASSWORD = os.getenv("NS_PASSWORD")
ROLE_INTERNALID = os.getenv("NS_ROLE_INTERNALID")

# TBA credentials
CONSUMER_KEY = os.getenv("NS_CONSUMER_KEY")
CONSUMER_SECRET = os.getenv("NS_CONSUMER_SECRET")
TOKEN_ID = os.getenv("NS_TOKEN_ID")
TOKEN_SECRET = os.getenv("NS_TOKEN_SECRET")


def soap_login():
    """Perform a simple SuiteTalk SOAP Passport login.

    Note: Many accounts use Token-Based Authentication in production. SOAP Passport
    might be disabled for your account. This shows the minimal envelope and POST.
    """
    if not all([ACCOUNT, EMAIL, PASSWORD]):
        raise SystemExit("Missing SOAP credentials (NS_ACCOUNT/NS_EMAIL/NS_PASSWORD)")

    endpoint = f"https://webservices.netsuite.com/services/NetSuitePort_{SOAP_VERSION}"

    role_fragment = ""
    if ROLE_INTERNALID:
        role_fragment = f"<platformCore:role internalId=\"{ROLE_INTERNALID}\"/>"

    envelope = f"""<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
                  xmlns:platformCore="urn:core_1dtypes.platform.webservices.netsuite.com"
                  xmlns:urn="urn:messages_{SOAP_VERSION}.platform.webservices.netsuite.com">
  <soapenv:Header/>
  <soapenv:Body>
    <urn:login>
      <urn:passport>
        <platformCore:email>{EMAIL}</platformCore:email>
        <platformCore:password>{PASSWORD}</platformCore:password>
        <platformCore:account>{ACCOUNT}</platformCore:account>
        {role_fragment}
      </urn:passport>
    </urn:login>
  </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>"""

    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "text/xml;charset=UTF-8",
        "SOAPAction": "login",
    }

    r = requests.post(endpoint, data=envelope.encode("utf-8"), headers=headers)
    print("SOAP endpoint:", endpoint)
    print("Status:", r.status_code)
    print("Response (truncated):", r.text[:1000])

    if r.status_code != 200 or "<soap:Fault" in r.text:
        raise SystemExit("SOAP login failed")

    # In a real implementation extract the sessionId and consume it for subsequent SOAP calls.
    return r.text


def tba_request():
    """Perform a small REST GET authenticated with OAuth1 (Token-Based Authentication).

    Requires: requests and requests_oauthlib installed.
    """
    if not all([ACCOUNT, CONSUMER_KEY, CONSUMER_SECRET, TOKEN_ID, TOKEN_SECRET]):
        raise SystemExit("Missing TBA credentials (account and consumer/token keys/secrets)")

    # Base REST domain for SuiteTalk REST endpoints (account-specific)
    base = f"https://{ACCOUNT}.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/rest/record/v1"

    # Example: list first few customers (depending on account role/permissions)
    url = f"{base}/customer"

    # NetSuite expects OAuth 1.0 signatures. The signature method may vary by account.
    oauth = OAuth1(client_key=CONSUMER_KEY,
                   client_secret=CONSUMER_SECRET,
                   resource_owner_key=TOKEN_ID,
                   resource_owner_secret=TOKEN_SECRET,
                   signature_method='HMAC-SHA256')

    r = requests.get(url, auth=oauth, headers={"Accept": "application/json"})

    print("TBA REST URL:", url)
    print("Status:", r.status_code)
    print("Response (truncated):", (r.text or '')[:1000])

    if r.status_code not in (200, 201):
        raise SystemExit("TBA request failed")

    return r.json()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if AUTH_METHOD == "SOAP":
        soap_login()
    elif AUTH_METHOD == "TBA":
        tba_request()
    else:
        raise SystemExit("Set NS_AUTH_METHOD to SOAP or TBA in environment")
